### [Anthropic Economic Index: Insights from Claude 3.7 Sonnet](https://www.anthropic.com/news/anthropic-economic-index-insights-from-claude-sonnet-3-7)

**Anthropic** · 2026-08-25

Anthropic released its second Economic Index report, analyzing 1 million Claude.ai conversations post-launch of Claude 3.7 Sonnet alongside a new 630-category bottom-up usage taxonomy.

- Extended thinking mode usage was highest in technical and creative fields, led by computer and information research scientists (~10%), software developers (~8%), multimedia artists (~7%), and video game designers (~6%).
- Analysis of 1 million anonymized Free and Pro conversations using the privacy-preserving tool Clio showed modest usage increases in coding, education, and science occupational categories.
- Anthropic released a bottom-up dataset covering 630 granular usage categories and a dataset mapping O*NET tasks to their corresponding extended thinking mode fractions on Hugging Face.

**Why it matters:** The released datasets and usage trends provide granular empirical data on how advanced capabilities like extended thinking and agentic coding are actively deployed across technical labor markets.

### [Introducing the Anthropic Economic Index](https://www.anthropic.com/news/the-anthropic-economic-index)

**Anthropic** · 2026-08-25

Anthropic launched the Economic Index, utilizing a privacy-preserving automated tool named Clio to analyze approximately one million Claude.ai conversations mapped to standard U.S. Department of Labor occupational tasks.

- Used 'Clio', an automated analysis tool, on approximately one million anonymized Claude.ai Free and Pro conversations to preserve user privacy while evaluating real-world AI usage.
- Mapped conversation topics directly to O*NET, the U.S. Department of Labor database containing around 20,000 specific work-related tasks.
- Found 'computer and mathematical' occupations (software engineering, code debugging, network troubleshooting) accounted for the largest share of queries at 37.2%.
- Identified 'arts, design, sports, entertainment, and media' as the second-largest query category at 10.3%, primarily driven by writing and editing tasks.
- Open-sourced the underlying dataset to allow external economists and researchers to analyze real-world task augmentation and automation.

**Why it matters:** Analyzing direct usage data mapped to official labor task classifications provides an empirical baseline for understanding how AI augments or automates specific economic roles.

`ai-economics` `labor-market` `claude` `dataset` `anthropic`

### [Funding better evaluations of AI’s impact on wellbeing](https://www.anthropic.com/news/wellbeing-research-grants)

**Anthropic** · 2026-08-25

Anthropic launched a $5 million grant program to fund independent, open-source research and evaluations on how AI affects user wellbeing.

- Grantees receive direct funding, model access, and technical support to build open-source evaluations and benchmarks for the broader AI industry.
- The initiative targets complex multi-turn conversational contexts, such as emotional support, companionship, mental health crises, and history of disordered eating, where single-turn evaluation is insufficient.
- Anthropic is involving multidisciplinary experts, including clinicians, psychologists, and methodologists, to establish standardized safety evaluations.
- Applications close on September 21, with selected full-proposal applicants notified by October 5.

**Why it matters:** It supports the creation of standardized, open-source benchmarks to detect and evaluate complex, long-context wellbeing risks across AI platforms.

### [Launching the Anthropic Economic Futures Programme in the UK and Europe](https://www.anthropic.com/news/economic-futures-uk-europe)

**Anthropic** · 2026-08-25

Anthropic is expanding its Economic Futures Programme to the UK and Europe, offering research grants, Claude credits, granular usage data, and a inaugural policy symposium at the London School of Economics.

- The programme provides UK and EU researchers with research grants, Claude credits, and granular data regarding actual AI deployment.
- Data from the Anthropic Economic Index shows regional Claude usage patterns: academic research/writing in the UK, equipment calibration/repair in German manufacturing, and four times the global average for tourism/culture queries in France.
- Coding is identified as the most common overall use case for Claude across the European continent.
- The initiative launched with a joint symposium at the London School of Economics and Political Science (LSE) featuring open-call policy proposal presentations.

**Why it matters:** Empirical data and targeted research grants will help European and UK policymakers construct informed labor and economic policies during rapid AI adoption.

**Hugging Face** · 2026-08-25

Quantization-Aware Healing compresses models to 4-bit precision while attempting to maintain or improve performance compared to the original full-precision baseline.
